text.p: Kuwaiti police seized 29,532 unlicensed weapons including three multiple rocket launchers between August 1992 and January 1995, newspapers said on Thursday.

A list presented by Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah to a parliamentary commission also showed 181 rocket launchers, 25 surface-to-air missiles, 4,200 automatic rifles and 51 anti-aircraft guns, they said.
The weapons were apparently among thousands left by Iraqi troops after the 1991 Gulf War that ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of Kuwait.
In 1994 parliament banned police from raiding private residences to search for weapons, citing fears that raids could be abused by the police, deputies said.
Newspapers said Sheikh Khaled was pushing for parliament's approval of a bill to reinstate police searches for weapons.
Diplomats said Kuwait was concerned that weapons kept by residents could be smuggled to neighbouring countries for what they described as potential terrorist attacks.
